copies.headline: Noah's Receivers Vanish, Adam Stays Perfect
copies.body:
Wideouts decided this. Adam got 39.7 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Chris Olave; Noah got 15.6 from Garrett Wilson and Michael Wilson, both of whom missed projection by roughly six and a half apiece. That 24.1-point gap at receiver is almost exactly the final margin, which tells you everything about the other positions canceling each other out — Colston Loveland's 18.5 and Drake Maye's 23.8 were real edges that went nowhere because Rhamondre Stevenson turned 13.3 of projection into 3.6.
Adam won on his worst week of the year. He posted 132.7, a season low, with Mark Andrews contributing 1.4 and Bucky Irving coughing up nine points below projection, and still cleared Noah by three touchdowns on Kenneth Walker III's 27.9 and Tyler Bass outscoring Spencer Shrader by nearly ten. We called it by 21. Close enough.
Noah also benched Hunter Henry's 14.8 for Josh Downs and the Browns defense for the 49ers, which is 11 points he didn't need to leave anywhere. At 1-5 with an all-play of 20-46, he isn't unlucky — he's 11th in scoring. Adam, 6-0 and first in everything, remains boring in the most expensive way possible.

copies.headline: Logan's Spare Parts Bury John's Stars
copies.body:
The margin came from the places nobody drafts for. Germie Bernard put up 25.7 in Logan's flex, Isaiah Likely went for 23.9 at tight end, Chase McLaughlin kicked 18.6, and the Chiefs defense added 14 against a Jaguars unit that finished at negative two. That's four roster slots John lost by a combined 50-plus, which is the entire game. Logan's 152.5 is a season high and his third straight week climbing.
John's problem was the top of his lineup going quiet all at once. Kyren Williams managed 9.7 against a 21.0 projection, Puka Nacua 14.0 on 22.8, Brock Bowers 11.0 on 19.8. D'Andre Swift's 23 was the only starter who beat his number by much, and one running back can't cover a 52.4-point hole. We had John by 16, which aged about as well as the Jaguars defense.
John still scores 128.5 a game, second in the league, and is 41-25 on all-play — he's not broken, he just picked the worst week to be. Logan is 2-4 with the fifth-best scoring in the league and 1.5 wins of bad luck, which is a familiar kind of misery for a man who used to collect top seeds.

copies.headline: Isaac Starts Two Zeroes, Loses By 45
copies.body:
The running back room ended this before lunch. Christian got 24.7 from Bhayshul Tuten and 14.9 from Alvin Kamara; Isaac got 13.0 from Javonte Williams and a pair of actual zeroes from Cam Skattebo and Saquon Barkley in the flex. That's a 26.6-point hole at one position, and Jameis Winston turning 17.8 projected into 6.5 while C.J. Stroud put up 23.0 on the bench made it unrecoverable. Matt Gay outscoring Brandon Aubrey 11.5 to 1.0 was the only column Isaac won.
Christian didn't even need to be sharp. Pat Freiermuth missed by eight with Khalil Shakir sitting, Trevor Lawrence scored 27.3 in street clothes, and 124.3 still cleared the bar by 45. We had Christian by 14 and undersold it.
Both sit at 2-4, but only one deserves company there — Christian's 39-27 all-play is fourth in the league and 1.5 wins of bad luck. Isaac is 17-49 and last in scoring, which is its own kind of slap.

copies.headline: Pitts and McCaffrey Outrun Leif's Dead Weight
copies.body:
Leif won this at the two spots nobody drafts for: tight end and flex. Kyle Pitts put up 23.0, Christian McCaffrey put up 30.7, and that 13.6 and 18.6 edge covered a multitude of sins. And there were sins. Derrick Henry managed 5.0 on an 18.3 projection, Davante Adams gave back 6.9 on a 16.0, Josh Allen came in nearly seven under, and the Texans defense actively cost him two points. Grant won QB, RB, WR, kicker and defense and still lost by 6.8, which is the fantasy equivalent of losing a game you led in every category but points.
Grant's problem is that his ceiling arrives in installments. Nine starters, nobody above 18.5, Tony Pollard and Christian Watson both landing well short, and Keon Coleman's 15.9 watching from the bench instead of replacing Watson's 9.4. Leif had the same bench sin — Stefon Diggs 16.4 while Adams flopped — but Leif had McCaffrey, so it didn't matter.
Leif is 4-2 with an all-play of 40-26, third in the league in both scoring and deserved record; this isn't luck. Grant falls to 3-3 and is still winning slightly more than he's earned. We picked Leif by 16 and only missed because his flex did all the work alone.

copies.headline: CJ's Backfield Buries Mitchell's Empty Flex
copies.body:
The running backs settled this before anyone checked a box score. Jonathan Taylor and Chuba Hubbard combined for 40.2 while Mitchell got 17.5 out of Rachaad White and a Tyjae Spears performance — 1.8 points on an 8.7 projection — that qualifies as a rounding error. Add Tyler Shough outscoring Dak Prescott by 16 and the 39.9-point margin was already assembled by Sunday afternoon.
Mitchell actually won the receivers and won tight end by 9.3, which is remarkable given CJ started Juwan Johnson for a donut. It didn't matter, because DJ Moore gave him a zero in the flex with George Holani and his eight points watching from the bench, and Tyler Loop chipped in 3.4 at kicker. CJ won his own flex battle by leaving Emeka Egbuka's 17.8 unused, which is the kind of mistake you can afford at 4-2.
Mitchell is 1-5 with an all-play of 27-39 and minus-1.5 luck wins — he's scoring 7th and sitting dead last in the only column that counts. The human coin flip has landed tails five times.

copies.headline: Peter's Receivers Vanish, Kaleb Walks Away
copies.body:
Wideouts decided this one and it wasn't close. Kaleb got 31.2 from Drake London and Carnell Tate; Peter got 15.8 from George Pickens plus whatever Denzel Boston was doing — 2.5 points on a 13.5 projection, with Romeo Doubs and his 11.2 sitting on the bench. Add A.J. Brown at 5.7 against a 12.7 projection and Bijan Robinson turning a 23.0 projection into 7.3, and Peter's 69.8 is less a bad week than a full systems failure. Only Dameon Pierce and Tucker Kraft showed up.
Kaleb didn't exactly play a clean game either. Harold Fannin Jr. and Ladd McConkey combined for 4.6, and Tre Tucker put up 26.7 in street clothes. He didn't need any of it. Ashton Jeanty and RJ Harvey carried the backfield and the Bucs defense outscored Peter's entire receiving corps' worst two.
We picked Peter by 13, which looks generous now. Both sit 4-2, both are running hot on luck — Kaleb's all-play is 24-42 — but Peter's the one who went from 163.0 in Week 4 to this. The 2022 title keeps getting further away.

intro: Leif over Grant by 6.8 was the only game that required watching past the early window, and Logan's 152.52 was the week's high-water mark by a comfortable 20 points. On the other end, Peter's 69.78 was the lowest score of the slate by nearly 16, and Isaac's 78.98 wasn't far behind, which means two teams combined for less than Logan did by himself. Five of the six margins cleared 24 points, so if you were hoping for drama, you watched the wrong league this week.
